constraints: One to sixteen exact immutable bytes objects, each at most 65536 bytes; authenticate before hashing and preserve signed digest/kind/outcome in signed order.
Portable synchronous offline software contract, no I/O or content interpretation; no target hardware, deadline, measured bottleneck or throughput requirement.
alternatives: Python exact immutable inputs with native-backed hashlib SHA-256 and frozen metadata.
Rust sha2 with owned or safely borrowed stable inputs.
C#/F# SHA256.HashData span or byte-array APIs with explicit stable ownership.
Erlang/Elixir OTP crypto:hash with binary message data.
rationale: KEEP the bounded immutable input and native hash boundary. Each alternative supplies maintained SHA-256 APIs, but none alone preserves signed metadata or establishes a measured deployment improvement for this small stateless operation. No manual hashing, new data copy or streaming layer is required.

Hashlib can release the GIL on larger inputs, so exact immutable byte ownership matters independently of interpreter serialization. Read-only views in alternative hosts still require backing-storage ownership discipline.

The current code preserves all reference fields, but the prior ten evidence methods do not detect replacement of every kind with synthetic. One new real-signature test compares complete reference metadata after reversing supplied and signed order; it detects that mutation.
No runtime failure or winning migration is established. The correction is executable regression coverage, not language diversity or an unmeasured performance recommendation.
limits: Candidate APIs were inspected from current primary documentation; no full alternate binder or throughput comparison was executed.
One MiB limits input content, not process RSS. Digests can correlate guessable content and are not encryption or anonymization.
The binder authenticates signed assertions and matches bytes, not scientific truth, physical provenance, permissions or certification.
No lane completion, MLS/CNSA, hard-real-time, availability or physical qualification. Insufficient information for tactical deployment.
